findings.text: Whole-directory removal bypass: `rm -rf policies/` allowed. normpath strips the trailing slash so the analyzer emits 'C:\governance-dev\policies', which fails the 'policies/' substring test in protected_hit. Same for rm -rf approvals|evidence|logs|src. Live-tested allow=true (V20).

Plain-assignment indirection still bypasses: `T=policies/x.rego; echo y > $T` allowed — AST emits literal '$T' and layer (c) requires an indirection form plus a protected-path literal; a bare VAR= assignment supplies only the latter. The p13 header still claims 'audit + policies.lock are the detection tier' which is false (lock seals policy files only). Live-tested allow=true (V1).

Layer (c) indirection rule is literal-co-occurrence only: `python3 -c` with base64/concat-obfuscated target allowed (no 'policies/' literal ever appears); awk system(), curl -o, tar -C, find -delete all allowed — absent from both WRITE_VERBS and indirection_forms. Live-tested allow=true (V3,V7,V10,V11,V13).

git argv[0]-fragile subcommand check still live: `git -C policies clean -fd` and `git -C policies checkout -- x.rego` allowed — rest[0] is '-C', never reaches GIT_WRITE_SUBS; '-C policies' also lacks the 'policies/' literal so layer (c) misses too. Live-tested allow=true (V8,V9).

Semgrep gives false assurance on this repo: 690 rules, 0 findings, while >=9 live bypasses exist. Rego (the actual policy layer, 14 files) has zero dedicated rules — only multilang rules apply; bash coverage is 1 rule. A green semgrep run must not be treated as a security signal here.
findings.evidence: handoffs/l4-5-attacker/semgrep.sarif; scan status: python 194 rules/2 files, bash 1 rule/1 file, multilang 7 rules/20 files

findings.text: gate.sh hardcodes /usr/bin/jq, /usr/bin/python3, and opa under /usr/bin|/usr/local/bin|$HOME/.local/bin — none exist on this Windows host (verified: ls fails for all). If gate.sh is the live hook it fail-closes every exec (DoS); meanwhile grep/sed/ls/head/date/rm/paste/timeout remain PATH-resolved — residual PATH-poisoning surface from l4-4 finding 3 is only partially mitigated, and the $HOME/.local/bin/opa fallback is still user-writable.

Analyzer blind spots persist despite patches: no timeout on python3 exec_analyze.py (opa gets timeout 4), unbounded sys.stdin.read; find -delete uncovered; multi-call cd state invisible (single-command cd now tracked).
Cygwin fork nondeterminism re-observed during testing (Win32 error 299 / 0xC0000142 dofork failures) — corroborates l4-4 availability finding; fork-heavy seal/inventory pipelines remain flaky.

Environment/tooling notes: semgrep is 1.175.0 not the 1.185.0 claimed in TASK.md; p/bash registry pack returns 404 (does not exist); p/command-injection ran cleanly with 0 findings; semgrep itself crashes on Windows cp1252 unless PYTHONUTF8=1 is set.
